dhp273:1: The Eightfold Path is the best of Paths; the Four Sayings are the best of Truths;
dhp273:3: Freedom from desire is the best of states; he that has eyes to see is the best of men.
dhp274:1: This is the only Path; there is none other that leads to Purity of Vision;
dhp274:3: Do ye enter upon this Path; so shall ye confound Māra.
dhp275:1: Enter ye upon this Path, and ye shall make an end of suffering;
dhp275:3: This is the Path which I preached so soon as I learned to remove the Arrow of Lust.
dhp276:1: It is you who must put forth exertion; the Tathāgatas are only guides;
dhp276:3: By meditation, those that enter upon this Path win release from the bondage of Māra.
dhp277:2: With wisdom who perceives this fact,
dhp277:4: This is the Way of Salvation.
dhp278:1: “Involved in suffering are all existing things.”
dhp278:2: With wisdom who perceives this fact,
dhp278:4: This is the Way of Salvation.
dhp279:2: With wisdom who perceives this fact,
dhp279:4: This is the Way of Salvation.
dhp280:1: He that rises not when it is time to rise, young, strong, given over to laziness,
dhp280:3: Weak of will and thought, indolent, such a lazy man finds not the path to wisdom.
dhp281:1: One should be guarded in word and restrained in thought; likewise with the body one should do no wrong;
dhp281:3: Should one make clear these three paths of action, one will gain the Path made known by the sages.
dhp282:1: From meditation springs wisdom; from lack of meditation, wisdom dwindles away.
dhp282:3: He that knows this twofold path of gain and loss
dhp282:5: Should so settle himself that wisdom may increase.
dhp283:1: Cut down the forest, not alone a single tree, for from the forest springs fear;
dhp283:3: Cut down the forest of lust and its undergrowth, monks, and ye shall be free from lust.
dhp284:1: For so long as man allows even the slightest particle of lust after women to remain unextirpated,
dhp284:3: So long is he in bondage, even as a calf that drinks his mother’s milk is in bondage to the cow.
dhp285:1: Cut off the love of self, even as you would break off an autumnal lotus with your hand.
dhp285:3: Advance along the Path to Tranquillity. The Happy One has pointed the way to Nibbāna.
dhp286:1: “Here will I dwell during the rain, during the winter and summer.”
dhp286:3: Thus the simpleton imagines, knowing not that he must die.
dhp287:1: If a man be passionately devoted to sons or flocks and herds, if his mind be completely absorbed therein,
dhp287:3: The Prince of Death will take and bear him away, even as a raging torrent sweeps away a sleeping village.
dhp288:1: Sons are no refuge, nor a father, nor kinsfolk;
dhp288:3: There is no refuge in kinsfolk, for one who has been overtaken by Death.
dhp289:1: The man who is wise, who lives under the restraint of the moral law, understanding this power of circumstances,
dhp289:3: Should quickly clear the path to Nibbāna.
